title: Paged-attention slot reclamation and background decanting
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem:
Paged attention improvements have reduced per-token compute, but long-running tenant workloads and bursty decode waves produce fragmented KV residency across page slots. Fragmentation increases the number of page fetches during prefill and causes decode stalls when contiguous slots are not available. Current eviction heuristics are reactive and cause decode-induced thrash under mixed-length workloads.

Goal:
Introduce a low-cost background reclamation and "decanting" subsystem that periodically compacts lightly-used page slots into fewer pages and reclaims scattershot slots for reuse, while preserving decode latency SLOs and limiting tail impact. The system should be safe for live traffic, gated, measurable, and revertible.

Proposal (high level):
1) Slot heat classification: maintain a lightweight token-residency heatmap per-page (hot/warm/cold) derived from touch counts and decode wave timestamps. Heatmap is decayed epochally to avoid churn.
2) Safe-epoch markers: use epoch markers tied to in-flight decoders to ensure background compaction does not evict slots that will be imminently read by active requests. Compaction only touches pages whose last-safe-epoch < current-epoch - threshold.
3) Background decanting worker: a background thread (configurable concurrency) that performs micro-compactions: copy warm/cold slots into destination pages that have free contiguous ranges, update page metadata atomically, and mark source slots as reclaimed. The worker operates with bandwidth throttling and backoff to respect GPU memory bandwidth and cache-coherency windows.
4) Conservative reclamation policy: prefer reclaiming slots that free a minimum contiguous run length to benefit decode prefill. Avoid reclaiming small scattered slots unless a tenant is over quota.
5) Tenant-aware soft quotas: expose soft residency quotas per-tenant to avoid one tenant causing global fragmentation. When a tenant exceeds soft quota, decanting is allowed to be more aggressive for that tenant's pages.
6) Integration with kernel selector: mark pages compacted by the decanter with a "packed" hint so kernel-selection logic can prefer kernels optimized for contiguous KV layouts.
7) Safety and rollout: feature-flagged, start in read-only simulation mode (metrics only), then enable background-only (non-evicting copy + mark), then enable full reclamation in canary (10% traffic), ramp to 50% if metrics stable. Automated rollback on increased prefill stalls or p99 latency regressions.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Copying KV slots off-page requires atomic updates to page tables. We'll rely on existing paged-KV metadata versioning used by the prefetcher to avoid races.
- The microcompactor will batch copy operations to reduce kernel launch overhead. Batching parameters tuned in experiments.
- Conservative approach avoids moving hot slots; we use a decay window to prevent movements during tail-heavy sessions.
- Worst-case extra memory peak from destination pages must be constrained; we cap background worker's working set and coordinate with the allocator to pre-reserve temporary space.
- Alternative (rejected for now): in-place defragmentation that rewrites page layouts during decode; rejected due to risk of stalls and complex coordination with decoders.

Telemetry and success metrics:
- KV fragmentation ratio (free slot scatter score) should drop by >=30% in target workloads (mixed short+long sequences).
- Prefill stall events per 1M requests should drop by >=40% for medium-length sequences (512-2048 tokens).
- 95th and 99th decode latency should not regress more than 2% during rollout; immediate rollback if regress >5%.
- Memory overhead (peak working set) <= +8% during background compaction windows.

Experiment plan:
- Phase A: Simulation mode (metrics only) on canary hosts for 2 weeks with synthetic mixes.
- Phase B: Background copy+mark enabled (no reclamation) to validate metadata correctness.
- Phase C: Canary reclamation (10% traffic) for 1 week, evaluate metrics and errors.
- Phase D: Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% if stable; monitor customer-facing metrics.

Rollout and operational hooks:
- Console dashboard: new "KV compaction" panel showing fragmentation, compaction throughput, reclaimed slots, and rollback triggers.
- Runtime config: concurrency, minimum-run-length, heat-decay-window, per-tenant thresholds, bandwidth cap.
- Alerts: prefill-stall-rate increase, p99 decode latency regression, compaction error bursts.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (Confluence) describing algorithms and safety.
- Runtime PR implementing decanting worker and metadata changes.
- Console metrics + dashboards.
- Load-test comparisons and canary results.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation metric reduced by at least 30% on benchmark mixed workloads
Prefill stall rate reduced by at least 40% for medium-length request mixes
No more than 2% regression in p95/p99 decode latency during canary; automated rollback if >5%
Feature gated and deployable; design doc and runtime PR merged
Console panels and alerts created for compaction metrics
